skill: Ratios, Rates, Proportional Relationships, and Units
stem: A machine fills 91 bottles in 7 minutes. At this constant rate, how many bottles does the machine fill in 23 minutes?
explanation: The machine fills 91 / 7 = 13 bottles per minute. In 23 minutes it fills 13 × 23 = 299 bottles.

skill: Ratios, Rates, Proportional Relationships, and Units
stem: A recipe calls for 5 cups of broth for every 3 cups of rice. If a chef uses 11 cups of rice, how many cups of broth does the chef need?
explanation: The ratio of broth to rice is 5 to 3, so broth = (5/3) × rice. With 11 cups of rice: (5/3)(11) = 55/3 cups of broth. The value 33/5 results from inverting the ratio and using 3/5 instead of 5/3. The value 53/5 comes from a multiplication error when computing 5 × 11. The value 15/11 comes from setting the proportion incorrectly as 3/5 = rice/broth and further inverting.

skill: Ratios, Rates, Proportional Relationships, and Units
stem: A car travels 217 miles using 7 gallons of fuel. Fuel costs 3.89 dollars per gallon. At the same rate of fuel consumption, what is the fuel cost, in dollars, for a 589-mile trip?
explanation: The car uses 217 / 7 = 31 miles per gallon. For 589 miles the fuel needed is 589 / 31 = 19 gallons. Total cost is 19 × 3.89 = 73.91 dollars. The value 74.83 results from miscalculating 589 / 31 as approximately 19.236 and then multiplying by 3.89. The value 69.81 comes from dividing 589 by 217 to get approximately 2.71 and multiplying by 7 to get approximately 18.97 gallons, then rounding to 17.95 gallons times 3.89 — a unit-handling error. The value 76.07 results from rounding 589 / 31 up to 19.55 and computing 19.55 × 3.89.

stem: A store sells a jacket for 83 dollars. If the sales tax rate is 7%, what is the total cost, in dollars, of the jacket including tax?
explanation: The tax is 0.07 × 83 = 5.81 dollars. The total cost is 83 + 5.81 = 88.81 dollars.

stem: A population of 4,300 organisms decreases by 18% in the first year and then increases by 11% in the second year. What is the population at the end of the second year, rounded to the nearest whole number?
explanation: After the first year: 4300 × 0.82 = 3526. After the second year: 3526 × 1.11 = 3913.86, which rounds to 3914. The value 3526 results from applying only the first-year decrease and stopping there. The value 3999 comes from treating the net change as a single 7% decrease (18% minus 11%), giving 4300 × 0.93 = 3999, which incorrectly adds percentage changes instead of compounding them. The value 3698 results from an arithmetic error when multiplying 3526 × 1.11.

stem: An item's price was first increased by 30%, then decreased by $p$ percent, resulting in a final price that is 4.5% less than the original price. What is the value of $p$, rounded to the nearest tenth?
explanation: Let the original price be 1. After a 30% increase the price is 1.30. After a p% decrease the price is 1.30(1 - p/100). This equals 0.955 (which is 4.5% less than original). So 1 - p/100 = 0.955/1.30 = 0.73461..., giving p/100 = 0.26538... and p is approximately 26.5. The value 34.5 results from setting up the equation as 1.30 - p/100 = 0.955 (subtracting p/100 from 1.30 instead of multiplying by the factor). The value 25.5 comes from a rounding error when dividing 0.955 by 1.30. The value 30.0 comes from incorrectly assuming the decrease percentage equals the increase percentage.

skill: One-Variable Data: Distributions and Measures of Center and Spread
stem: A data set consists of the values 14, 19, 23, 23, 27, 31, and 38. What is the median of this data set?
explanation: There are 7 values listed in ascending order. The median is the 4th value (the middle value), which is 23.

skill: One-Variable Data: Distributions and Measures of Center and Spread
stem: A set of 9 test scores has a mean of 74. If a score of 53 is removed from the set, what is the mean of the remaining 8 scores?
explanation: The total of all 9 scores is 9 × 74 = 666. Removing the score of 53 gives a total of 666 − 53 = 613 for 8 scores. The new mean is 613 / 8 = 76.625. The value 74 assumes the mean is unchanged after removing a data point, which is only true if the removed value equals the mean. The value 77.375 results from dividing 619 by 8, an arithmetic error in the subtraction step. The value 73 comes from simply subtracting 1 from the original mean.

skill: One-Variable Data: Distributions and Measures of Center and Spread
stem: A teacher records quiz scores for 11 students: 41, 47, 52, 55, 58, 61, 63, 67, 71, 79, 93. The teacher decides to replace the highest score (93) with 71. Which of the following correctly describes the effect on the mean and median?

options.text: Both the mean and the median decrease.
The mean decreases and the median stays the same.
Both the mean and the median stay the same.
The mean stays the same and the median decreases.

explanation: The original sum is 41 + 47 + 52 + 55 + 58 + 61 + 63 + 67 + 71 + 79 + 93 = 687, with mean 687/11 ≈ 62.5. Replacing 93 with 71 reduces the sum by 22 to 665, so the new mean is 665/11 ≈ 60.5 — the mean decreases. The median is the 6th value in the sorted list. Originally: 41, 47, 52, 55, 58, 61, 63, 67, 71, 79, 93 — the median is 61. After replacement the sorted list is 41, 47, 52, 55, 58, 61, 63, 67, 71, 71, 79 — the 6th value is still 61, so the median stays the same. Claiming both decrease incorrectly assumes that lowering a value above the median shifts the median. Claiming both stay the same ignores that lowering a data value reduces the sum and therefore the mean. Claiming the mean stays the same while the median decreases reverses which measure is affected.

stem: A line of best fit for a scatterplot is given by $y = 2.3x + 11$. According to this model, what is the predicted value of $y$ when $x = 9$?
explanation: Substituting x = 9 into the equation: y = 2.3(9) + 11 = 20.7 + 11 = 31.7. The value 29.3 results from computing 2.3 × 9 as 18.3 instead of 20.7. The value 20.7 comes from computing 2.3 × 9 correctly but omitting the addition of 11. The value 33.7 results from computing 2.3 × 9 as 22.7 and then adding 11.

stem: A researcher collects data on the number of hours studied ($x$) and exam score ($y$) for several students and finds a line of best fit $y = 4.7x + 53$. What is the best interpretation of the slope 4.7 in this context?

options.text: For each additional hour studied, the predicted exam score increases by 4.7 points.
For each additional point on the exam, the predicted study time increases by 4.7 hours.
A student who studies 0 hours is predicted to score 4.7 on the exam.
The exam score is 4.7 times the number of hours studied.

explanation: The slope of a linear model represents the change in the predicted y-value for each one-unit increase in x. Here, for each additional hour studied, the predicted exam score increases by 4.7 points. Saying each additional exam point corresponds to 4.7 more hours reverses the roles of the independent and dependent variables. Saying a student who studies 0 hours scores 4.7 confuses the slope with the y-intercept (which is 53). Saying the score is 4.7 times the hours ignores the additive constant and mischaracterizes the relationship as purely multiplicative.

stem: A biologist models the relationship between average daily temperature in degrees Celsius ($t$) and the number of insect sightings ($n$) using $n = 1.9t - 18$. On a day when the temperature was 29 degrees Celsius, the actual number of sightings was 42. What is the residual for this observation?
explanation: The predicted value is n = 1.9(29) - 18 = 55.1 - 18 = 37.1. The residual equals actual minus predicted: 42 - 37.1 = 4.9. The value -4.9 results from computing predicted minus actual instead of actual minus predicted, reversing the sign. The value 37.1 confuses the predicted value itself with the residual. The value -37.1 both mistakes the predicted value for the residual and applies the wrong sign.
